item.title: Democratic Turek holds narrow lead in Iowa Senate race, internal polling shows
item.description:
Democratic state Rep. Josh Turek narrowly leads his Republican opponent, Rep. Ashley Hinson, in Iowa’s crucial Senate race, according to internal polling from the Democrat’s campaign first shared with Semafor. Turek is garnering 46% of the vote to Hinson’s 42%, while Libertarian candidate Thomas Laehn is getting 6%, and 6% of voters are undecided, according to the survey from Global Strategy Group conducted for Turek’s campaign. Those are notable numbers for Turek in a state dominated by the GOP for the past decade; Turek has an edge among independent voters and a positive favorability rating compared to Hinson, who is viewed more negatively. Another warning sign for the GOP: Trump is nine points underwater in Iowa, a state he’s won three times — including by 13 points in 2024. Most strategists see the race as a toss-up, though Hinson is narrowly leading most recent polls .

item.title: North Carolina cold case takes grim turn after remains identified as runaway 15-year-old girl missing since 1977
item.description:
Authorities announced a major breakthrough in a decades-old cold case, identifying human remains found nearly 49 years ago in North Carolina as belonging to a runaway 15-year-old girl who disappeared from Maryland. The skeletal remains were discovered more than six months after Cindy Marcell Blizzard went missing in the spring of 1977, according to the North Carolina State Bureau of Investigation (SBI). Authorities said the manner of death remained undetermined, but the case was being investigated as a homicide. They said the remains were found in a wooded area near a Wilson County manufacturing facility roughly five hours south of Blizzard's home. The "circumstances surrounding the location and recovery of the remains raised the probability of foul play, and the investigators are treating the case as a homicide," the SBI said.
